items.stem: Which of these can be separated by using a magnet?
items.markingKey: (a) Iron filings from sand.

items.stem: Which of the following is a pure substance?
items.markingKey: (c) Sugar is a pure substance. The others: sea water – a mixture; soil – a mixture; air – a mixture.

items.stem: Why is brass called a homogeneous mixture?
items.answer: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc mixed uniformly; the composition is the same throughout, though it can vary between samples.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: alloy of Cu and Zn. 1 mark: uniform.

items.stem: Which of the following is a homogeneous mixture?
items.markingKey: (b) Brass is a homogeneous mixture. The others: poha with peanuts – a heterogeneous mixture; soil – a heterogeneous mixture; oil and water – a heterogeneous mixture.

items.stem: Classify these mixtures as a heterogeneous mixture or a homogeneous mixture: air, sand in water, poha with peanuts, sugar solution.
items.answer: A heterogeneous mixture: poha with peanuts, sand in water. A homogeneous mixture: air, sugar solution.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A heterogeneous mixture: poha with peanuts, sand in water. A homogeneous mixture: air, sugar solution.

items.stem: A shopkeeper sells "pure ghee" that melts over a wide range of temperatures instead of at one fixed point. What can you conclude, and why?
items.answer: It is probably adulterated (a mixture); a pure substance melts at a fixed temperature, but a mixture melts over a range.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: mixture/adulterated. 1 mark: fixed melting point reasoning.

items.stem: Which of the following is a heterogeneous mixture?
items.markingKey: (b) Poha with peanuts is a heterogeneous mixture. The others: vinegar – a homogeneous mixture; sugar solution – a homogeneous mixture; salt solution – a homogeneous mixture.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A substance made of only one kind of particles, with the same composition throughout."
items.markingKey: (a) A pure substance is a substance made of only one kind of particles, with the same composition throughout.

items.stem: Plan how you would separate a mixture of salt, sand and iron filings, naming the property used at each step.
items.answer: Use a magnet to remove iron filings (magnetic); add water and stir to dissolve salt (solubility); filter to remove sand (insoluble); evaporate the filtrate to get salt.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct step with property (max 3).

items.stem: Which of the following is a homogeneous mixture?
items.markingKey: (b) Vinegar is a homogeneous mixture. The others: sand in water – a heterogeneous mixture; poha with peanuts – a heterogeneous mixture; soil – a heterogeneous mixture.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Air is a pure substance.
Reason (R): Air contains nitrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide and other gases.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false; R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which element has the symbol N?
items.markingKey: (d) N stands for nitrogen.

items.stem: Which elements combine to form common salt (sodium chloride) (NaCl)?
items.markingKey: (d) Common salt (sodium chloride), NaCl, is made of sodium and chlorine.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The symbol of sodium is So.
Reason (R): Some symbols come from Latin names of elements.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false (Na, from natrium); R true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following is a compound?
items.markingKey: (a) Water is a compound. The others: brass – a mixture; muddy water – a mixture; milk – a mixture.

items.stem: Classify these substances as an element or a compound: oxygen, helium, sulphur, carbon dioxide, common salt.
items.answer: An element: helium, oxygen, sulphur. A compound: carbon dioxide, common salt.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): An element: helium, oxygen, sulphur. A compound: carbon dioxide, common salt.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a mixture?
items.markingKey: (c) Ammonia is a compound, not a mixture. Each of the others (muddy water, milk, tea) is a mixture.

items.stem: Classify elements as metals, non-metals and metalloids. Compare metals and non-metals on any four physical properties, and give two uses each of metals and non-metals.
items.answer: Metals: copper, iron; non-metals: sulphur, oxygen; metalloids: silicon, boron. Metals are lustrous, malleable, ductile, sonorous, good conductors; non-metals dull, brittle, poor conductors (except graphite). Uses: copper wires, aluminium foil; oxygen for breathing, chlorine for purifying water, carbon as fuel.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: classification; 2 marks: comparison; 2 marks: uses.

items.stem: Why is water called a compound and not a mixture of hydrogen and oxygen?
items.answer: Hydrogen and oxygen combine chemically in a fixed ratio (2 : 1 by atoms) to form water, whose properties are completely different from those of the two gases.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: chemical combination in fixed ratio. 1 mark: new properties.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A pure substance made of only one kind of atoms that cannot be broken into simpler substances by chemical methods."
items.markingKey: (c) An element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atoms that cannot be broken into simpler substances by chemical methods.

items.stem: Which of the following is an element?
items.markingKey: (d) Helium is an element. The others: tea – a mixture; common salt – a compound; brass – a mixture.

items.stem: Which of the following is a mixture?
items.markingKey: (c) Tea is a mixture. The others: ammonia – a compound; common salt – a compound; water – a compound.

items.stem: The chemical symbol of sulphur is:
items.markingKey: (b) Sulphur: S.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Hydrogen is a compound.
Reason (R): Hydrogen gas is made of molecules.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false; R true (H₂ molecules of one kind of atom).
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Which of the following is a compound?
items.markingKey: (d) Common salt is a compound. The others: soil – a mixture; tea – a mixture; carbon – an element.

items.stem: Which is a property of a compound?
items.answer: Its elements are in a fixed ratio by mass
items.markingKey: (b) Its elements are in a fixed ratio by mass.
options: Its elements are in a fixed ratio by mass
Its components can be separated by a magnet

items.stem: Distinguish between a compound and a mixture on the basis of energy change and separation.
items.answer: Energy change: compound – Heat/light usually given out or absorbed; mixture – Usually no energy change; Separation: compound – Only by chemical methods; mixture – By physical methods like filtration, magnet, evaporation
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct point of difference.

items.stem: Why does iron sulphide not get attracted by a magnet, though iron does?
items.answer: Iron sulphide is a compound with new properties; the iron in it is chemically combined and no longer behaves like free iron.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: compound. 1 mark: new properties.

items.stem: Distinguish between a compound and a mixture on the basis of composition and properties.
items.answer: Composition: compound – Fixed ratio of elements; mixture – Any ratio of components; Properties: compound – New properties, different from those of its elements; mixture – Components keep their own properties
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct point of difference.

items.stem: Distinguish between a compound and a mixture on the basis of composition and energy change.
items.answer: Composition: compound – Fixed ratio of elements; mixture – Any ratio of components; Energy change: compound – Heat/light usually given out or absorbed; mixture – Usually no energy change
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct point of difference.

items.stem:
Read: In a lab, Ishaan made two samples. Sample P: iron filings and sulphur powder stirred together. Sample Q: the same mixture heated strongly till it glowed and turned into a black solid.
(i) Which sample is a compound? (ii) What happens when a magnet is brought near each? (iii) Why did Q glow? (iv) Can sulphur be dissolved out of P using carbon disulphide?
items.answer: (i) Q (iron sulphide). (ii) P: iron filings attracted; Q: not attracted. (iii) Heat is given out when a compound forms. (iv) Yes, sulphur in a mixture keeps its property of dissolving.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Ammonia gas is made of nitrogen and hydrogen, both of which are odourless gases. Ammonia has a sharp smell. What does this tell us about compounds?
items.answer: A compound has properties different from those of the elements that form it.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: new properties. 1 mark: reasoning.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Iron sulphide is attracted by a magnet.
Reason (R): Iron sulphide contains iron.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A false; R true—but combined iron does not show magnetism here.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Bhavna has two white powders: one is a mixture of sugar and salt, the other is pure sugar. Suggest two simple tests to tell them apart.
items.answer: Taste a tiny bit (under supervision): the mixture is sweet and salty in parts; heat both: pure sugar melts at a fixed temperature, the mixture does not (salt remains). Also dissolve and test the solution for conduction: salt solution conducts.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per valid test (max 2) + 1 for reasoning.

items.stem: Define ductility.
items.answer: The property of being drawn into thin wires
items.markingKey: 1 mark: Ductility – the property of being drawn into thin wires.

items.stem: Silicon is used in computer chips because it is a:
items.markingKey: (a) metalloid that is a semiconductor.

items.stem: Why are school bells made of metal?
items.answer: Metals are sonorous; they produce a ringing sound when struck.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: sonorous. 1 mark: ringing sound.

items.stem: Classify these elements as a non-metal or a metal: gold, sulphur, aluminium, iodine.
items.answer: A non-metal: iodine, sulphur. A metal: aluminium, gold.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A non-metal: iodine, sulphur. A metal: aluminium, gold.

items.stem: Which of the following elements is NOT a metal?
items.markingKey: (a) Germanium is a metalloid, not a metal. Each of the others (aluminium, gold, mercury) is a metal.

items.stem: Mercury is a metal but is used in thermometers. Which two properties make it suitable?
items.answer: It is a liquid at room temperature that expands evenly on heating, and it is shiny, so its level is easy to see; it is also a good conductor of heat, so it responds quickly.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per property (max 2).

items.stem: Which term is described here? "An element that is usually hard, shiny, malleable, ductile and a good conductor of heat and electricity."
items.markingKey: (c) A metal is an element that is usually hard, shiny, malleable, ductile and a good conductor of heat and electricity.

items.stem: You are given three unlabelled rods: copper, a graphite rod and a sulphur stick. Suggest tests to identify each using a hammer and a battery-bulb tester.
items.answer: Copper: shiny, flattens on hammering, conducts. Graphite: dull grey, brittle but conducts. Sulphur: yellow, brittle, does not conduct.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct identification with test.

items.stem: Classify these elements as a metalloid or a non-metal: phosphorus, germanium, boron, nitrogen, silicon, oxygen.
items.answer: A metalloid: boron, germanium, silicon. A non-metal: nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): A metalloid: boron, germanium, silicon. A non-metal: nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Sulphur is used to make electric wires.
Reason (R): Sulphur is a non-metal and is brittle.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.

options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Which elements combine to form methane (CH₄)?
items.markingKey: (d) Methane, CH₄, is made of carbon and hydrogen.

items.stem: Classify these substances as a mixture or an element: milk, air, oxygen, helium, brass.

items.stem: Distinguish between a compound and a mixture on the basis of properties and separation.
items.answer: Properties: compound – New properties, different from those of its elements; mixture – Components keep their own properties; Separation: compound – Only by chemical methods; mixture – By physical methods like filtration, magnet, evaporation
